🚀 Core Challenge & Solution

NASA's upcoming SPHEREx all-sky spectral survey will observe millions of celestial sources every 6 months. Detecting bona fide transients, cometary outbursts, moving asteroids, and candidate sub-stellar worlds (Planet X) requires rigorous passband matching, automated subtraction, and defensible uncertainty budgets. AFTERLIGHT provides an end-to-end scientific platform solving this challenge.

NASA Challenge 12: Planet X and SPHEREx
🔬 Key Scientific Pillars
  • Task-Specific Compatibility: Strict mathematical gating before difference imaging.
  • Defensible Measurements: Explicit uncertainty propagation budgets (mJy, arcsec).
  • Structured Evidence Ledger: Traceable claims linking observations, FITS WCS, & provenance.
  • Cosmos AI Assistant: Multi-mode scientific reasoning grounded in genuine archive data.
Full Compliance with NASA / IPAC IRSA Workflows

Frontend Engineering & User Experience

🌌 4D Relativistic Minkowski Physics Engine
  • Proper Time Evolution: Continuous tracking of relativistic proper time τ in seconds.
  • Lorentz Dilation Factor: Real-time physics calculation of γ = 1 / √(1 - v²/c²).
  • Doppler Shifting: Approaching stars blueshifted (#7dd3fc); receding redshifted (#f472b6).
  • Spacetime Worldlines: Dynamic Minkowski geodesic constellations connect guide stars.

Slide 4 / 7 • Backend Engineering

Backend Architecture & Scientific Engines

FastAPI Asynchronous Engine with Rigorous Astronomical Auditing and Uncertainty Quantification

⚖️ Compatibility Auditor

Enforces strict physical gates before temporal subtraction: checks central wavelength shift (Δλ ≤ 20%), zero-point spectrophotometric ties, and Gaia DR3 WCS sub-pixel co-registration (RMS < 0.12″).

Class: TaskCompatibilityAuditor
📐 Measurement & Uncertainty

Computes defensible astronomical observables: source flux difference (ΔF = +0.32 ± 0.07 mJy, 5.8σ), centroid motion vector (Δr = 0.84 ± 0.09″), and 3-component uncertainty budgets (shot, calibration, background).

Class: ScientificMeasurementEngine
🔎 Autonomous Discovery Sifter

Executes autonomous multi-epoch filtering across SPHEREx DR1 catalogs, identifying high proper-motion planetary candidates, cometary vapor outbursts, and variable pulsating stars.

Endpoint: POST /api/sifter/run
Slide 5 / 7 • Observational Data

Data Architecture & SPHEREx Contracts

Real NASA SPHEREx DR1 Data Models, FITS Provenance, and Standardized Schemas

🛰️ SPHEREx Instrument Parameters
  • Wavelength Coverage: 0.75 to 5.00 μm across 102 continuous spectrophotometric channels.
  • Detector Arrays: 6 detector arrays (InSb & HgCdTe) utilizing Linear Variable Filters (LVF).
  • Spatial Sampling: 6.2 arcsec/pixel, 145×145 px cutouts centered on deep-field tangents.
  • Cadence Baseline: 6-month survey repeats enabling high proper-motion parallax detection.
NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) Standard
📊 Structured Evidence & Case Contracts
  • ObservationRecord: Normalized observational metadata (ID, date, λ, detector, units).
  • EvidenceRecord: 4-pillar data contract (Observed, Measured, Interpretation, Unknown).
  • CaseRecord: User hypotheses, audit trails, and scientific peer review ledger.
  • UncertaintyBudget: Statistical error, PSF kernel mismatch, and zero-point calibration error.
Standardized Multi-Epoch JSON Data Models
